en: (At the end of the *nāndī*, the *sūtradhāra* enters.
*Sūtradhāra*:
The world of the nether regions (*pātāla*), where the throngs of women, men, *danuja*s, and *suparvan*s are struck with confusion upon beholding the man-lion’s (*nara-mṛgapati*) form...
May Śrīdhara—the destroyer of the hosts of the enemies of the gods, whose chest was split by the edge of the thunderbolt born from his own hand—be for your prosperity. || 1 ||
(Offstage) Ho there!
Ho there! Let it be announced, let it be announced to the Great King, the Lord of Aṅga! Director:
Let it be known:
when the tumultuous battle had begun, a servant, agitated and with palms joined in reverence, reported to Karṇa by the command of Duryodhana. || 2 ||
(He exits. The Prologue. (Then enters a soldier.)
Soldier:
Ho there! Let it be announced, let it be announced to the Great King, the Lord of Aṅga, that the time for battle has arrived!
[Let it be proclaimed] by those mounted on elephants, horses, and chariots before the banner of Pārtha.
Today, a lion’s roar has been let out by the joyful lion-like kings;
Nāgaketu, whose valor is unbearable for his enemies to behold, having achieved his purpose in battle, sets forth amidst the swift clamor of his foes. || 3 ||

(Walking about and looking around) Ah! Here is the King of Aṅga, surrounded by his martial retinue, emerging from his own palace along with King Śalya; he is approaching right here. Oh! Why indeed is there such unprecedented anguish in the heart of this man, who is foremost in the festival of battle and whose prowess has been witnessed?
For he is preeminent in combat, radiant with most fierce splendor.
And now, though possessed of wisdom, he approaches his valor with sorrow;
like the sun, naturally radiant yet obstructed by a mass of clouds when the summer season has arrived, so does Karṇa appear. || 4 ||
"I shall now withdraw.
(Exit.
(Then enter Karṇa and Śalya as described.)
Karna:
Let it not be that these kings, having become the targets for the path of my arrows, should reach this point with their lives still remaining.
Whatever must be done at the head of the battle, let that be performed for the sake of the Kurus, provided that Dhananjaya may be seen by me. || 5 ||
O King Śalya! Let my chariot be directed right to where that Arjuna is.
Śalya:
Very well. (He urges him on.
Karṇa:
Alas! Indeed,
when in great battles— where warriors, horses, elephants, and chariots have their limbs mangled by the falling weapons of one another—
at the time of combat, even in my mind, which possesses a prowess like that of the enraged God of Death, a sense of despondency arises.
Alas, what misery!
Previously born of Kuntī, I am known as Rādheya;
yet Yudhiṣṭhira and the others are my younger Pāṇḍava brothers. || 7 ||
This is that time when beauty is naturally attained; this day has arrived, the pinnacle of all virtues.
Yet, alas, I have mastered weapons in vain.
And again, he was restrained by his mother’s words. || 8 ||
"O King Śalya, listen to the account of my weapon.
Śalya:
"I too have a great curiosity to hear this account."
Karṇa:

I went to the presence of the son of Jamadagni long ago. Śalya: [What did he say? Karṇa: He said this: "O King, you must know that I have already been defeated by Arjuna in battle. Śalya: [How so? Karṇa: Listen, O King, I shall tell you exactly as it happened. Once, while I was practicing with my bow on the banks of the Yamunā, Arjuna arrived there. Having seen me, he spoke these words: "O Kṣatriya, why do you practice with your bow? I shall show you how to fight; come, let us engage in combat. Then, having heard those words, I laughed and said to him: "O Kṣatriya, I am not afraid of you. Fight me if you are able! Then, having heard my words, he took up his bow and arrows and challenged me to battle. Thereupon, we engaged in a wrestling match, and I threw him down upon the ground. Then, having been thrown down, he rose up and seized my feet with both hands. While he was thus seizing my feet, I struck him with my knee and killed him. When he had been killed, I departed from that place. Then, having heard that I had been killed, Arjuna’s mother Kuntī wept aloud. Then, having heard her lamentation, I went to her and spoke these words: "O Queen, do not weep; I am alive. Know that I have killed Arjuna in battle. Then, having heard my words, she embraced me and said: "O son, you have performed a great deed today. You have indeed slain your enemy in battle. Then, having comforted her, I departed from that place. This is what occurred between me and Arjuna. Therefore, O King, you must know that I have already been defeated by Arjuna in battle. Śalya: [Excellent! Well said, O son of Rādheya! Karṇa: Furthermore, O King, listen to another thing that occurred between me and Arjuna. Once, while I was practicing with my bow on the banks of the Gaṅgā, Arjuna arrived there. Having seen me, he spoke these words: "O Kṣatriya, why do you practice with your bow? I shall show you how to fight; come, let us engage in combat. Then, having heard those words, I laughed and said to him: "O Kṣatriya, I am not afraid of you. Fight me if you are able! Having approached and bowed to that best of sages, the banner of the Bhṛgu lineage and the destroyer of the Kṣatriyas, whose mass of lofty matted hair is tawny like streaks of lightning and who bears an axe encircled by rising radiance, I now stand nearby in silence. (9)
Śalya:
And then?
Karṇa: [And then...]
Then I was questioned by the son of Jamadagni, who asked: "Who are you, and for what purpose have you come here?
Shalya said:
"And then? And then?"
Karna:
Then, O Blessed One, I said, "I wish to learn all the weapons. Shalya: [Continues:]...
And what happened next?
Karṇa said: "Then I was told by the Blessed One: 'I shall bestow instruction upon the Brāhmaṇas, but not upon the Kṣatriyas.'"
Śalya:
Indeed, there was formerly an enmity between the Blessed One and those of the Kṣatriya lineage. What happened after that?
Karṇa:
"Therefore, thinking 'I am not a Kshatriya,' I began to refuse instruction in weapons.
Shalya:
"And then? And then?"
Karṇa:
Then, after some time had passed, on one occasion, I went along with my elder brother who had gone out to gather fruits, roots, sacrificial fuel, kusha grass, and flowers.
Śalya: [Continues]...
I, too, have a curiosity to hear this account.
Karṇa:
I myself previously went into the presence of the son of Jamadagni.
Śalya:
And then?
Karṇa: [And then...]
Then,

having approached and prostrated before that best of sages— the banner of the Bhṛgu lineage and the destroyer of the Kṣatriyas— who bore a mass of high matted locks tawny as a flash of lightning and held an axe encircled by rising radiance, I stood nearby in silence. (9)
Śalya:
And then? Then what? Karṇa: [Continues]...
Then I was questioned by the son of Jamadagni: "Who are you, and for what purpose have you come here?
Śalya:
And then? What happened next?

Then, O Blessed One, I said, "I wish to learn all the weapons. Shalya: [Continues]...
And what happened next?
Karṇa said: "Then I was told by the Blessed One: 'I shall impart instruction to the Brāhmaṇas, but not to the Kṣatriyas.'"
Śalya:
Indeed, there was formerly an enmity between the Blessed One and those of the Kṣatriya lineage. What then? What then? Karṇa:
"Therefore, thinking 'I am not a Kṣatriya,' I began to refuse the instruction in weapons.
Śalya:
"And then? And then?"
Karṇa:
Then, after some time had passed, I once went along with my preceptor, who had gone out to gather fruits, roots, sacrificial fuel, kuśa grass, and flowers. Śalya: [Continues]...
And then?
Karṇa:
Then that preceptor, exhausted by the fatigue of wandering through the forest, fell under the power of sleep upon my lap.
Śalya:
And then?
Karṇa: [And then...]
Then,
when my finger was cut by a worm named Vajramukha, which had come by chance to obstruct me, I endured the pain through the teacher's fortitude and out of fear of interrupting his sleep.
Rising up suddenly, drenched in blood and inflamed by the fire of his wrath, he recognized me and cursed me, saying: "May your weapons be rendered fruitless by Time! (10)

Let us first examine the history of this weapon. (Having done so) these weapons appear as if they have lost their power. Moreover, these horses have their eyes closed in dejection, repeatedly stumbling, and are utterly helpless.
And the elephants, smelling of the ichor from the *saptacchada* tree,
seemed as if they were announcing a retreat from the battle.
The conch shells and drums fell silent.
Śalya said: "Oh, what misery! What indeed is this?"
Karna:
O King Shalya! Enough, enough with this despondency!
Even if slain, one attains heaven; but by conquering, one attains glory.
Both are highly esteemed in the world; there is no fruitlessness in battle.
Moreover,
these horses, whose hope never retreats in battles, possess a speed equal to that of Suparṇa.
May those born into the illustrious Kāmboja lineages protect me, even though they themselves ought to be protected. (13)

May there be inexhaustible merit for cows and Brahmins; may there be inexhaustible merit for women devoted to their husbands; may there be inexhaustible merit for warrior-men who do not turn their backs in battle; and may there be inexhaustible merit for me, whose time has come. O sir, I am pleased;
having entered the unbearable front of the Pāṇḍavas' battle.
Having bound Dharmarāja, who is enriched by a multitude of celebrated virtues,
and having struck down Arjuna with the force of my excellent arrows as if he were a lion slain in the forest, I shall make it easy to enter.
"O King Śalya! Let us mount the chariot.
Śalya replied, "Very well."
(Both mime mounting their chariots.
Karṇa:
O King Śalya! Let my chariot be driven right to where that Arjuna is.
(Offstage) O Karṇa! I beg of you a most generous alms. (O Karṇa! I beg of you a most generous alms.
Karṇa—
(Listening) Ah, this is the sound of one possessed of great prowess!

This is surely not merely an eminent brahmin, for his power is immense. Having heard his deep-toned voice, my horses—whose bodies seem thrilled with wonder, whose ears are pricked, whose eyes are fixed, and whose necks are turned as they cast their faces forward—stand with their slender frames rendered helpless, even as they were suddenly moving along. (15)
"Let that Brahmin be summoned. "No, no! I myself shall summon him. Venerable sir, this way, this way! (Then Śakra enters in the form of a Brahmin.
Śakra:
O clouds! May you depart, having been turned back by the sun itself. (Approaching Karṇa) O Karṇa! I beg of you a most significant boon. (O Karṇa! I beg of you a most significant boon.
Karṇa:
I am deeply pleased, O Blessed One!
I have today attained the status of one who has fulfilled his purpose in this world, my lotus-feet honored by the crest-jewels of the lords of kings,
and my head purified by the dust from the feet of the foremost of Brahmins.
I, Karṇa, here pay homage to you. || 16 ||

Śakra—(To himself) What indeed should I say? If I say, "May you be long-lived," he will become long-lived. If I do not say it, he will despise me as a fool. Therefore, avoiding both outcomes, what exactly shall I say? Very well, I have found a way. (Aloud) O Karṇa!
May your fame endure like the sun, like the moon, like the Himavat, and like the ocean!
Karṇa:
Blessed One! What else could be said but "May you live long"? Or rather, this alone is most excellent. Why?
Because dharma is indeed to be accomplished by a person through diligent efforts.
The splendors of kingship are as fickle as the tongues of serpents;
therefore, when bodies have been sacrificed with the sole intention of protecting the subjects, virtues alone remain.
"Blessed One, what do you desire? What shall I give?
Śakra said:
"I ask for a greater alms-offering. (I ask for a more magnificent gift.)
Karṇa:
I shall bestow upon you a most generous gift. Hear of my wealth:
it rains down streams of milk that are like nectar and possess all virtues.

O best of the twice-born! I give you a thousand cows that are pleasing to you, accompanied by their contented calves, young, exceedingly desirable to supplicants, pure, and provided with golden horns. 18.

Śakra: "A thousand cows? I shall drink milk for a moment. I do not wish it, Karṇa! I do not wish it! Karṇa: [Repeats: "A thousand cows? I shall drink milk for a moment. I do not wish it, Karṇa! I do not wish it! Karṇa: [Continues:]...
What is it that you do not desire? Listen to this as well:
a mount equal to the sun’s horses, a source of royal fortune, honored by all kings, and born of the noble Kamboja breed.
I shall immediately give you many thousands of horses, endowed with excellent qualities, possessing the speed of the wind, and having displayed their prowess in battle. || 19 ||
Śakra: It is a horse! I shall mount it for a moment. I do not wish it, Karṇa! I do not wish it! (It is a horse! I shall mount it for a moment. I do not wish it, Karṇa! I do not wish it! Karṇa:
What does the Blessed One not desire? Listen to something else as well:
[his face] with cheeks streaming with rut-fluid, frequented by bees, resembling a mass of excellent mountains, and possessing a voice as deep as a thundercloud.
I give this multitude of elephants with white claws and tusks, which have repeatedly crushed their enemies in battle.
Śakra: "Gaja!
I shall mount for a moment. I do not wish it, Karṇa! I do not wish it!
(Gaja! I shall mount for a moment. I do not wish it, Karṇa! I do not wish it!)
Karna:
Why do you not wish for it? Listen to something else as well: I shall give you gold that is inexhaustible.
Śakra: [Silent.]
[Taking him] I go. (Having gone a little way) I do not wish it, Karṇa! I do not wish it! [Taking him] I go. I do not wish it, Karṇa! I do not wish it!
Karṇa:
In that case, having conquered the earth, I shall give it to you.
Śakra:
What shall I do with the earth? Karṇa: [listens]...
"Therefore, I grant you the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.
Śakra said:
"What is to be done with the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma?"
Karna:
In that case, I give you my head. Śakra: [Accepts.]
"Avihā! Avihā! ("Do not fear! Do not fear!
Karṇa:
"You must not be afraid, you must not be afraid. May your honor be appeased. Listen to something else as well."
Born together with my very limbs, this armor for my body cannot be pierced even by the great weapons of gods or asuras;
nevertheless, let this armor be given along with the two earrings.
Out of affection, I have [offered this] to the Blessed One, should it be pleasing to him. || 21 ||
Śakra:
(With joy) Give, give!
Karṇa:

(To himself) This is indeed his desire. What indeed could be the stratagem of Kṛṣṇa, whose intellect perceives many deceptions? Let it be so. Fie on grieving for what is improper! There is no doubt. (Aloud) Take it!
Śalya:
O King of Aṅga! It must not be given, it must not be given!
Karna:
O King Shalya! Enough, enough with this dissuading! Behold, through the passage of time, even skill goes to ruin.
The trees fall with their roots firmly established;
the water remains in its reservoirs and does not dry up; and likewise, that which is offered in sacrifice and given in charity endures.
Therefore, take it. (Having cut it off, he gives it.

Śakra—(Taking it, to himself: Ah, these have been obtained! That which was previously resolved upon by all the gods for the sake of Arjuna’s victory has now been accomplished by me. Therefore, I too shall mount Airāvata and witness the duel between Arjuna and Karṇa. (Exit.)
Śalya:
O King of Aṅga! You have indeed been deceived.
Karṇa:
By whom?
Śalya:
By Śakra.
Karna: Indeed not! It was Śakra himself who was deceived by me. Why?
Because he is the one adorned with a diadem, gratified by the twice-born with the oblations of numerous sacrifices, and the crusher of the hosts of Dānavas.
"Surely the subduer of Pāka has achieved his purpose, for my fingers have become calloused from striking the island of Suradvīpa. (23)
(Entering in the form of a Brahmin) The Messenger of the Gods:

O Karṇa! You have been favored by Purandara, who was moved by remorse for having taken your armor and earrings. Accept this infallible weapon, a spear named Vimalā, for the purpose of slaying a single preeminent hero among the Pāṇḍavas.
Karṇa:
Fie! I do not accept what has been given.
Devadūta:
"But surely, let it be accepted on the word of the Brahmin.
Karṇa said:
"On the word of a Brahmin? I have never before transgressed that. When shall I obtain [the earrings]?"
The divine messenger said:
"Obtain it whenever you remember.
Karṇa said:
"Very well; I am favored. May you return.
The divine messenger:
"Very well. (He exits.)

Karṇa:
Ah, a sound is heard! What indeed could this be? It is the blast of a conch shell, equal to the roar of the ocean at the time of universal dissolution;
it must belong to Kṛṣṇa, and not to Phālguna.
Surely Pārtha, his soul incensed by the defeat of Yudhiṣṭhira, will today fight according to his full strength.
"O King Śālva! Let my chariot be directed right to where that Arjuna is!
Śalya replied, "So be it."
(Bharata-vākya) May there be prosperity everywhere and may calamities perish forever;
may a single king, endowed with royal virtues, rule over our land. (25)
(They both exit.
The Karṇabhāra is finished.
